mbm-2826.clue: The rewind button has a crown.
mbm-2826.quote: In our anime club whoever spots a favorite painted background first gets to call rewind. We made a foil crown for the remote. At the end of a good episode the crown is covered in fingerprints.

mbm-2827.clue: My rook wears a tea stain.
mbm-2827.quote: The park table has a mug ring on the corner square. I always start my rook inside that circle. My best opponent tells me the rent is overdue whenever he captures it.

mbm-2828.clue: Everybody knows which ring belongs to the kitchen.
mbm-2828.quote: I do a linking-ring trick with two polished hoops and the iron ring from an old pudding mould. The kitchen ring sounds different when it drops onto the mat. My dad always claps before anyone else sees that it's free.

mbm-2829.quote: I liked the bright seams on the inside of a work shirt more than the outside. I sewed the next one with those seams showing and a plain pocket over my heart. Mum recognized her stitching from across the street.

mbm-2830.clue: Two seams cross where the old shops met.
mbm-2830.quote: I made a quilt from my father's blue shop apron and our neighbor's green one. Their stores shared one wall for thirty years. My sisters line up the blue-green seam when they fold it.

mbm-2831.clue: My running route has one quiet mile.
mbm-2831.quote: I turn off my little cassette player when I reach the old wooden bridge. The boards make a low beat under my shoes. On the other side I always have to turn the song up to match it.

mbm-2832.clue: The triangles point toward the windows.
mbm-2832.quote: I quilted a curtain for our tiny flat using scraps from our first year's clothes. In the morning the sun shows every seam through the cloth. My friend says the room gets dressed before we do.

mbm-2833.clue: The best square is still on the wrong quilt.
mbm-2833.quote: My neighbor and I accidentally swapped one square at a quilting bee. We noticed halfway through and kept sewing. When she brings her quilt over we put them side by side to visit.

mbm-2834.clue: I know exactly where to put the red book.
mbm-2834.quote: In my favorite sunny patch the wind tries to lift one corner of the beach mat. I set a thick red paperback there. If somebody borrows it I insist they stay and hold the mat down while they read.

mbm-2835.clue: I bring flour to the flying field.
mbm-2835.quote: My daughter once pressed a balsa glider into a tray of flour to see the shape of its wings. Now our plane-spotting scrapbook has floury white silhouettes beside my ink drawings.

mbm-2836.clue: The missing die made us kinder.
mbm-2836.quote: We lost the die during a train ride. Instead of rolling, each player moved forward as many stops as they could name along the line. We helped the youngest so much she arrived home first.

mbm-2837.clue: Our forecast fits in the palm of my hand.
mbm-2837.quote: Our flying club uses a row of little flags along the grass strip. The morning before Dad flew us home, every flag pointed somewhere different. He made a paper pinwheel for me and we walked the whole strip with it until I could feel what the flags were saying.

mbm-2838.clue: We gave the paddle its own sketch.
mbm-2838.quote: My canoeing friend draws people and I draw landscapes. On our longest trip we both sketched the same battered paddle. His leans one way and mine leans the other. Put the pages side by side and you can tell where each of us sat.

mbm-2839.clue: Our scoreboard is a pair of sandals.
mbm-2839.quote: One sandal points toward the water and one toward the shore. We slide a pebble up the strap for every volleyball point. On crowded days spectators have to ask permission before they put on the score.

mbm-2840.clue: I putt left-handed on the last hole.
mbm-2840.quote: My grandfather taught me mini golf with his old left-handed club. It feels wrong to finish with anything else. The windmill keeps a left-handed secret every time we visit.

mbm-2841.clue: My kayak has a little copper sunrise.
mbm-2841.quote: I pressed an old copper washer into my map case as a marker for our launch beach. In the morning sun it lights up before the horizon on the paper. I always know which way is home.

mbm-2842.clue: Our alley has a generous slope.
mbm-2842.quote: My favorite bocce lane curves down toward a grape arbor. A ball toward the arbor comes back slowly by itself. After a close game my aunt lets us leave the measuring cord and pick grapes.

mbm-2843.clue: The conductor wrote one small cloud.
mbm-2843.quote: At the station I asked the retiring driver to sign my sketchbook. He drew a puff of smoke beside the train instead of his name. Anyone who knows him can tell it's his.

mbm-2844.clue: I sunbathe in a patch of apricots.
mbm-2844.quote: My grandmother dried apricots on a tray beside the chairs outside. We sat in the sun together and turned the fruit when we turned a page. I won't rush a good book or a good apricot.

mbm-2845.clue: The brown patch has its own grain.
mbm-2845.quote: I quilted a cloth checkerboard and added one square from my carpenter aunt's old apron. It has a permanent little sawdust mark. My cousins always choose that side of the board.

mbm-2846.clue: My best afternoon came apart in twenty pieces.
mbm-2846.quote: I took a little jigsaw onto the lawn to do in the sun. A breeze tipped the board and dropped all the blue sky in the grass. I lay there warm on my elbows, finding bits of sky between the daisies. I didn't bother to finish the edges.

mbm-2847.clue: My model's cape used to clean glasses.
mbm-2847.quote: I cut a scrap from a soft purple lens cloth for my robot's cape. It hangs better than the stiff plastic one. My brother says the galaxy's cleanest robot is finally dressed for the job.

mbm-2848.clue: I learned my harmony from the busy signal.
mbm-2848.quote: Our phone made a low humming note between calls. I stood in the hall matching it until my sister needed the line. Now I can find that note in any room, even one without a telephone.

mbm-2849.clue: The spare seat watches our shoes.
mbm-2849.quote: At folk dance we put a chair in the center for the piper's coat. One morning the smallest dancer set her doll on it. That quiet little judge has watched every turn since.

mbm-2850.clue: I count the brushstrokes on the way home.
mbm-2850.quote: I pick a tiny patch of one museum painting and sketch the separate strokes I can see. On the bus I close the notebook and try to remember how a curve and a few yellow strokes became a lemon.
